d: Talabat is part of the Delivery Hero Group, the world’s pioneering local delivery platform, our mission is to deliver an amazing experience—fast, easy, and to your door. We operate in around 65 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Delivery Hero has been listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange since 2017 and is part of the MDAX stock market index.

As an Account Manager at Talabat (Qatar), you will be responsible for managing and growing relationships with our restaurant and vendor partners. You will serve as the main point of contact, helping them optimize their presence on our platform, grow their sales, and ensure a high level of partner satisfaction.
Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with existing restaurant and vendor partners.
Ensure high partner satisfaction and retention through proactive communication, support, and service excellence.
Serve as a trusted advisor, providing partners with insights that support their business growth on the platform.
Analyze sales, operational, and engagement data to identify areas for improvement in menu performance, pricing, promotions, and delivery logistics.
Share actionable recommendations based on performance metrics to drive revenue and efficiency.
Conduct regular business reviews to align on results, opportunities, and growth plans.
Identify growth opportunities within the portfolio – upsell services, suggest cross-promotions, and improve partner performance.
Support partners in optimizing content (e.g., menu structure, images, delivery times) for better customer engagement and conversion.
Recommend and coordinate marketing campaigns and promotional offers to drive order volume.
Collaborate closely with internal teams such as Marketing, Logistics, and Operations to address partner needs and resolve issues promptly.
Ensure smooth onboarding, campaign execution, and issue resolution for assigned accounts.
Negotiate and renew commercial agreements to ensure a fair and strategic partnership.
Ensure partners comply with service-level agreements and maintain operational standards, including delivery quality and availability.
q: 2+ years of experience in Account Management, Sales, or Partner Success (experience in food tech, FMCG, or e-commerce is a plus).
Strong analytical skills; comfortable working with data dashboards and Excel/Google Sheets to analyze performance and generate insights.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
Customer-first mindset with a strong focus on delivering value to partners.
Self-starter with the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.
Fluency in Arabic Language is a must

d: Echelon contracts continuously: a portfolio of technology partners on structural, programme and referral agreements, MOUs and term sheets with defence and energy technology companies, customer Scopes of Work delivered by our forward deployed teams, and a share plan that reaches every employee.

We are looking for a qualified hands-on lawyer — admitted to practice, with the training that comes with it — who has drafted and negotiated the contracts behind technology and AI delivery services, understands how those businesses work, and has the head for it: one who would rather be the only counsel in the room than one of twenty. The legal function grows next year; you will have shaped how it works before it does.
q: A hands-on lawyer who reads fast, drafts clean and marks uncertainty rather than inventing a position. You find contracts interesting because of what they make possible, not because of what they prevent.
Curiosity: You want to understand the deal before you paper it: where the value sits, what the partner actually wants, what the technology does. You hold the position that protects it.
Speed of learning: An unfamiliar instrument — a share plan, a referral agreement, a defence MOU — comes back from you as a workable draft, not as a list of questions.
Ownership & pace: A file is yours from first draft to signature. You turn a term sheet in days and keep the corporate record current without being asked.
Judgement: Pragmatic on commercial points, immovable on the ones that matter. You escalate the right things and explain why in three sentences.

Where you are: A qualified lawyer — a law degree and admission to practice are required — based in Saudi Arabia or the UAE, with hands-on experience of delivery-services contracting — Scopes of Work, master services and subcontracting agreements — and a working understanding of the technology and AI sector; fluent legal drafting in English, with Arabic spoken and written. What you have closed counts for more than how many years you have been closing.
r: You will run the day-to-day legal work of the group: drafting, negotiating and closing under the group’s standards, keeping the corporate house in order, and working with the General Counsel and external counsel on the matters that need them. The growing part of that work is services contracting: Echelon sells the expertise and time of its engineers, and the master services agreements, Scopes of Work, rate cards, staffing and subcontracting agreements under which they are deployed are heavily negotiated contracts the group signs. You will draft them, negotiate them and close them. Under the Delegation of Authority the CEO is the only signatory, so the quality of what reaches his desk is the whole of the job. Partnerships with technology companies require a different discipline: referral, revenue-share and reseller agreements, IP boundaries and exclusivity terms that must protect Echelon’s margin and position over the life of the relationship, not only the length of one engagement.

You will carry files from first draft to signature, hold Echelon’s positions on exclusivity, margin protection and first right of refusal for our forward deployed teams, and decide what needs the General Counsel and what does not. The method exists; you own the outcome inside it and decide the sequencing and the trade-offs, so that most files close on standard paper and the exceptions get the attention they deserve.

Services contracting: Master services agreements, Scopes of Work, rate cards, and staffing and subcontracting agreements for our engineering services business — with customers, with the partners we deploy for and with the firms we deploy alongside. Large, recurring contracts, often negotiated on the other side’s paper: you draft, negotiate and close them.
Partner & commercial contracting: NDAs, MOUs, term sheets, referral and revenue-share agreements, from first draft to signature through the DoA signature process.

Templates & playbooks: The recurring instruments — partner referral agreement, Partner Revenue Share terms, Scope of Work, NDA, employment contract and amendment — so that most files close on standard paper.

Corporate housekeeping: Board and shareholder resolutions, registers, the shareholders’ agreement and the share plan documentation for the holding company and the Saudi operating company, with the GNRC.

Employment & regulatory: Contracts, performance-bonus amendments, policies and Saudi labour-law compliance with the People function; the regulatory perimeter around data, licensing and, with Echelon Defense Industries, clearance-bound activity.
Intellectual property: Engineering IP held at group level, partner IP boundaries in every deployment, and the protection of Echelon-developed capability as it is productised.
x: Customer first: You measure your work by customer outcomes, and prioritise accordingly.
Ownership mentality :You own outcomes end to end. When something breaks or stalls, you treat it as yours to fix.
Clear communicator: You explain complex systems simply, to operators and executives alike, and make the value of your work visible.
Comfortable with ambiguity: You make progress with incomplete information, partial data and unfamiliar environments, and you enjoy solving problems where there is no structure yet.
Long-term builder: You invest in Echelon’s long-term success, bringing field insight back into our strategy and operations.
Location: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia; open to candidates based in Saudi Arabia or the UAE
Reporting: Echelon CEO; dotted line to Echelon’s holding Legal Counsel department
Package: A base salary with housing and education allowances, medical cover, and equity through the employee equity programme. Terms are shared at offer stage.
You start from the problem, not the precedent. You meet an unclear brief or an unfamiliar instrument with energy and a plan.
Curiosity: You learn how the business and its technology really work, and keep learning as the deals and the law move.
Speed: You move from brief to workable draft quickly and do not wait for perfect conditions.
Rigour: You check before you rely, read every clause you put forward for signature and can explain every position you take.
Confidence & humility: You challenge and accept challenge, and change your view on evidence, without ego.
Autonomy: You decide with incomplete information and own it; from an outcome, you organise the work yourself.
Resourcefulness: Missing documents, partial facts, an unfamiliar jurisdiction: you find a way with what is available.
Situational leadership: You lead when the moment calls for it, and follow when someone else has the better call.
A force multiplier: Your templates, playbooks and clear guidance make every team you work with faster.
AI-native practice: AI tools are part of how you research, draft and review, and you know where their output needs a lawyer’s check.

d: Ready to shape entity-level financial and regulatory reporting with rigour and pace?

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world. Guided by our purpose of opening up a world of opportunity, our ambition is to become the world’s most trusted bank globally, putting customers at the heart of everything we do.
This role manages entity-level financial accounting, financial control, operational accounting and Group and regulatory reporting activity.

It exists to ensure accurate, timely and effective financial and regulatory information is delivered in line with IFRS, applicable GAAP and Group and local regulatory requirements. The remit covers end-to-end reporting, close procedures, accounting policy and day-to-day Finance operations at optimal cost.

Success means consistently high-quality financial statements and regulatory returns, well-controlled processes and a strong internal control environment. You’ll partner closely with the CFO, business stakeholders and senior management to support decision-making and strengthen governance. You’ll also identify opportunities to improve processes and automate manual activity to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
q: A full-time graduation degree can be essential for obtaining a visa and/or work permit for Bahrain.
Minimum 3-5 years of work experience in Finance and overall post qualification experience of 3-5 years.
Proven experience preparing and reviewing Financial and Regulatory reports under IFRS and applicable GAAP in a regulated environment.
Demonstrate practical experience producing accurate and timely regulatory returns and responding to regulator requests
Show strong capability across entity-level close processes including design and operation of effective close procedures
Bring hands-on knowledge of accounting policy, operational accounting and transactional finance activities
Apply strong analytical skills to interpret and communicate financial and management information to support profitability and operational effectiveness targets
Demonstrate experience maintaining a strong control environment including reconciliations, general ledger governance and fixed-asset accounting
Evidence experience reviewing and testing key controls, risk-rating processes and establishing action plans where controls need strengthening
Bring established stakeholder management experience with senior management, front-office teams and support functions
Demonstrate experience managing resources across budgets and employees within a Finance reporting and operations remit

This role sits at the heart of how the entity reports its performance and meets its regulatory obligations. You’ll set the standards for accurate financial statements, dependable returns and well-controlled Finance operations. The work has clear visibility with senior management and relies on effective partnership across the business and support functions. If you’re looking to take ownership of end-to-end reporting, close and controls in a regulated environment, this is a chance to make that impact at scale.
r: Prepare and review financial statements in line with IFRS, applicable GAAP and Group and local regulatory requirements
Ensure accurate and timely submission of financial and regulatory returns including ad hoc requests from the Central Bank of Bahrain/NBR/Govt
Maintain robust close procedures to enable timely preparation and submission of financial statements
Ensure financial transactions are recorded in line with FIM requirements, IFRS and local GAAP
Partner with the business to develop value-added financial solutions and influence operating boards and stakeholders on financial matters
Maintain the integrity of financial and non-financial records through reconciliations, general ledger maintenance, fixed-asset accounting, internal control reviews and cash applications
Oversee delivery of Group and regional returns including Flash returns through planning, review and coordination across departments
Identify opportunities to improve processes, automate manual activities and strengthen the efficiency and effectiveness of Finance operations
Escalate control weaknesses, operational risks and regulatory issues promptly and implement agreed recommendations from auditors and regulators

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment.

We believe diversity brings benefits for our customers, our business and our people. Different ideas and perspectives help us innovate, manage risk and grow the business in a sustainable way. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.
Issued by The Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited.

d: Siemens Mobility (SMO) is the world’s leading provider of mobility solutions that enable the efficient, safe, and environmentally friendly transport of people and goods—helping to improve the quality of everyday life for millions worldwide.

Motivated by innovation, we develop intelligent solutions for the growing digitalization of the transport sector. Our offerings include rail vehicles, rail automation, road traffic management systems, rail electrification, and services.

In Oman, Siemens Mobility is delivering the signaling, telecom, and power supply systems for the 303 km Abu Dhabi-Sohar railway, which marks the first cross-country railway network in the Middle East, connecting the UAE and Oman.

Today, we are recruiting for a Site EHS Officer to join our team in Oman. This is an excellent career opportunity for professionals looking to join a truly international team in one of the biggest projects of Siemens Mobility.
r: Act as the key contact for Health, Safety, and Environmental matters at the assigned project sites, ensuring compliance with Siemens EHS principles, project requirements, contractual obligations, and applicable local and international regulations.
Conduct regular site inspections, identify potential EHS risks and non-compliance issues, and define, implement, and monitor appropriate corrective and preventive measures.
Support the implementation and maintenance of ISO 45001 Occupational Health & Safety Management System and ISO 14001 Environmental Management System requirements across the project.
Monitor compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety legislation and ensure that relevant requirements are effectively implemented on site.
Prepare detailed EHS reports covering inspection findings, audit results, incidents, corrective actions, performance indicators, and overall compliance status.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of EHS performance metrics, incidents, near misses, training, inspections, audits, and regulatory submissions.
Ensure that incidents and near misses are properly reported, investigated, documented, and followed up, including root-cause analysis and implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
Monitor the EHS performance of subcontractors and consortium partners, conduct assessments, provide feedback, and escalate significant non-compliance to the EHS Manager and Project Manager.
Support the Project Manager and EHS Manager in obtaining and maintaining required EHS permits, authorizations, certificates, and regulatory notifications.
Review subcontractor Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), Risk Assessments, and Permit to Work (PTW) documentation to ensure compliance with project and EHS requirements.
Ensure that EHS requirements and the project EHS plan are clearly communicated to employees, subcontractors, and other relevant stakeholders.
Conduct and record safety meetings, toolbox talks, site inductions, and other EHS communication activities.
Develop and maintain the EHS training matrix, identify training needs, and ensure completion of mandatory internal and third-party EHS training requirements.
Conduct emergency response drills in accordance with the approved project schedule and support continuous improvement of emergency preparedness.
Monitor EHS KPIs and targets, support project audits, and develop corrective action plans to address identified gaps.
Liaise with customers, contractors, regulatory authorities, consultants, and other stakeholders on EHS matters in coordination with the Project Manager and EHS Manager.
Support the identification and management of environmental risks, including requirements related to controlled or declarable substances used on the project.
Respond to emergencies, incidents, and near misses and coordinate with relevant emergency response teams to minimize impact and ensure appropriate follow-up.
Share lessons learned and best practices and contribute to the continuous improvement of EHS processes, procedures, and initiatives.
Support the evaluation of contractors' EHS performance and provide relevant feedback to the Project Procurement Manager and EHS Manager.
What Do I Need to Qualify for This Job?
Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, preferably Electrical, Civil, or a related discipline.
3 to 5 years of experience in Health, Safety & Environment, preferably within construction, infrastructure, installation, or railway projects.
NEBOSH IGC certification, with a Merit pass achieved before 2022.
Lead Auditor certification in ISO 45001 and ISO 14001.
Basic or Advanced First Aid certification.
Valid Oman/GCC driving license is mandatory.
Practical knowledge of Permit to Work (PTW) systems for installation activities in both greenfield and brownfield environments, including online and offline processes.
Strong knowledge of incident investigation processes, including root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and preparation of detailed investigation reports.
Good understanding of EHS risk assessment, mitigation measures, and health and safety best practices.
Experience in railway projects is considered an advantage.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively with multicultural teams and lead by example in promoting a strong EHS culture.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and operate effectively in challenging site environments.
Strong presentation skills with the ability to communicate EHS requirements, present performance data, and influence stakeholders.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office and other relevant computer applications.
CertIOSH or equivalent professional EHS membership is considered an advantage.
Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Knowledge of additional regional languages, including Hindi, is considered an advantage.
Willingness and ability to travel frequently between project locations and work in challenging site conditions as required.
